# Model and request factory performance

## Reproducing the profile

FactoryProf is opt-in and loads after Rails so its Fabrication adapter can see
and patch Fabrication. Use it only on bounded model or request paths:

```sh
FPROF=1 script/benchmark_model_specs \
  spec/models/account_spec.rb \
  spec/models/status_spec.rb \
  spec/models/user_spec.rb

FPROF=1 script/benchmark_request_specs spec/requests/api/v1/statuses
```

The benchmark scripts fix the seed at `12345`, report slow examples, and refuse
paths outside their respective spec types. Do not benchmark the entire suite in
one invocation. System and streaming specs are outside this profiling scope.

## August 2026 findings

The high-volume fabricators had unrelated implicit side effects:

- Every `:user` created two `LoginActivity` rows.
- Every `:status` created a `Bookmark`. Since the bookmark's default account was
  not the status author, that also created a second local account and user, and
  the user then created two login activities.
- The default account username and user email invoked Faker despite only
  requiring valid unique values.

These defaults made a status factory create a large graph whose login history
and bookmark were irrelevant to nearly all examples. Tests that exercise those
features already use the dedicated `:login_activity` and `:bookmark`
fabricators explicitly. The implicit callbacks were removed, while all
fabricator names and spec call sites remain unchanged. High-volume identity
fields now use deterministic Fabrication sequences.

## Measurements

RSpec execution time excludes Rails boot. Measurements used seed `12345` and
identical paths before and after the factory changes.

| Sample | Examples | Before | After | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Core models (`account`, `status`, `user`) | 256 | 7.41s | 5.95s | -19.7% |
| API v1 status requests | 75 | 5.19s | 3.67s | -29.3% |
| Combined samples | 331 | 12.60s | 9.62s | -23.7% |

A post-change FactoryProf run over the core model sample recorded 514 factory
calls taking 3.97s of 5.88s total process execution. The API v1 status request
sample recorded 339 calls taking 1.85s of 3.84s. This leaves account/status
creation as a useful future profiling target, but those remaining records are
part of the requested object graphs rather than unrelated factory history.

## Validation

Validation was performed directory by directory, never as a whole-suite run:

- All 1,795 model examples passed: each nested `spec/models` directory and the
  root model files were separate runs.
- All 1,877 request examples passed: each immediate `spec/requests` directory
  and the root request files were separate runs.
- A sequence smoke test created 100 users with valid unique identities and no
  implicit login activities.
- Focused bookmark, login activity, and account cleanup behavior passed.
- RuboCop reported no offenses in all changed Ruby files.

System and streaming specs were not run or modified.
